title: Shuffle
name: shuffle

source.title: Mini tutorial video. How to shuffle/cuttingshapes #tutorial #shuffledance

arc:
Cutting-shapes basic, danced light and high on the balls of the feet. The engine is the hips: every weight change starts as a small pelvic drop onto the landing foot, and the shoulders answer a beat late. Arms are loose and reactive — they are thrown by the torso, never placed. Hair and the hem of the dress are the follow-through: if they settle on the same frame the body does, the frame is dead.

Frames 0-7, the running-man half. Frame 0 is the loop's home pose, a wide neutral stance — plant it flat, it is also the landing from 31. By frame 2 the feet have already left the floor, so the anticipation is spent before the torso finishes leaning character-right; frames 3 and 7 are the airborne extremes, 7 the highest point of the whole cycle. Land each step in the knee, not the ankle, and keep the character-left hip riding high through 2-5 — that lifted hip is what sells the scissor.

Frames 8-17, recovery. Weight crosses to character-left through 9, then 11 and 15 are the only rests in the cycle. Play them as real stops with a residual bounce left in the supporting knee, not as frozen frames. The character-right arm folds up to a bent guard across 13-15 and stays there while the legs restart — that arm carries through the next phrase rather than resetting.

Frames 18-31, the crossing steps and the throw. The character-right knee folds progressively 18-20, tightest at 20 (the pilot), with the leg passing behind the standing leg — the depth block calls the far limb on 19, 20, 23 and 25, so draw the crossing leg behind, never guessed. Frame 21 is the hit pose: wide, knee at 90, both arms live. 23 mirrors the cross the other way on tight feet, 27 is the second airborne extreme with the character-right arm thrown overhead, and 30-31 fall back toward the home stance. The seam needs a blend: 31 is airborne and 0 is planted, so the last step lands into frame 0 rather than cutting to it.
